[Messages]
[client]: I’ve been doing my best to actually use the couple of things we picked out as this week gets busier.

Having specific response windows and that little 60-second reset before I open my inbox has made some parts of the day feel more contained, like I’m choosing my focus instead of just reacting. I’ve also tried a quick 3-minute review in the evening, and seeing even a short list of “this went okay” has helped take a tiny bit of the edge off the “you’re failing” chorus.

That said, my body still feels like it’s on high alert most of the time, especially whenever a new "big push" reminder or "on top of things" message comes through. I can feel that wired/foggy state kick back in, and even if I know logically I’m not dropping everything, I still don’t fully trust that if I relax my grip at all I won’t miss something important.

Since it seems like we’re coming to the end of this conversation, I wanted to say that it’s been a relief to actually lay this out with someone instead of just white-knuckling it alone. From everything we’ve talked about, what would you suggest I literally write down or stick somewhere I’ll see it, so I’m more likely to remember these habits and thought checks when things get loud again? And if (or when) I slip back into old patterns, how would you suggest I respond to myself in that moment so it doesn’t instantly become more “evidence” that I can’t handle things?
rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Structuring reminders and responses**

I'm thinking about where to place reminders: on my phone lock screen, as sticky notes on my laptop, or even setting calendar events with pop-up reminders at the end of the day. If I experience any slips, I’ll have a brief script to respond with self-compassion, saying something like, "That's the critic—one reset, one step." It's helpful to reframe a slip as data, noting triggers and adjusting my approach. I could also offer support by asking if someone would like a formatted note to easily copy and paste.
rounds.response:
Nice to hear it’s helped a bit—here’s a short, copy‑ready set to stick where you’ll see it: Response windows: 9:30 / 1:30 / 4:30 (DND outside these); Escalation = deadline <24h OR blocks a top priority OR flagged client; 60‑sec reset = hand to chest, 3 slow breaths, name the critic, ask “one concrete next step?”; Evening 3‑min review = 1 win + what actually needed attention + tomorrow’s top priority.  
Put that on your phone lock screen, a sticky on your laptop, a pinned note in Slack, or as a calendar event title at the start/end of day so it’s visible when you need it.  
If you slip, try this micro-script: “That’s the critic—one reset, one step,” do the 60‑sec reset, and then pick the smallest possible next action (treat the slip as data, not proof).  
If the same triggers keep causing slips, note the trigger briefly and tweak the rule or window (small experiments over time beat one big perfect plan).  
Want me to draft a single-line lock‑screen or Slack pin you can paste in now?
